name: start.me
tagline: A customizable browser start page of bookmark widgets, notes, RSS feeds and search boxes.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a grid of links, some notes, a weather box and a few RSS feeds, rendered on page load. There is no network effect: your start page is valuable because your links are in it, and an agent can build that shell in an afternoon. The hard parts are cosmetic, drag-and-drop tiles, favicon fetching, a tolerable dark theme, and all of them are solved problems with libraries. Self-hosting also fixes the actual objection to hosted start pages, which is that your entire browsing map lives on someone else's server. What you give up is convenience: no browser extension that saves the current tab in one click, no mobile app, no team sharing.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted start page with multiple tabs, drag-and-drop widget columns of bookmarks, notes and RSS feeds, stored in a local SQLite file and importable from a browser bookmarks export.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to run it, local machine or a small VPS
A browser bookmarks HTML export if you want your existing links in on day one
Optional: any small box or container host so the page is reachable from other devices
whatYouLose: The browser extension that saves the current tab into a chosen widget with one click
Real mobile apps and a start page that loads instantly on a phone
Hosted sync and backups across devices without you running anything
Public and shared start pages, team spaces, and the admin bits around them
Automatic dead-link checking and the polished widget library, weather, calendar, stocks, and so on
moatNotes: The lock-in is habit, not technology: once a start page is your browser homepage on four devices, moving costs an evening.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a start page is the one app you look at fifty times a day, and fifty-times-a-day apps must never be broken, slow or down. Paying means the extension, the mobile layout, the sync and the backups are somebody else's problem, and the widget catalog already covers the thing you were about to want. A self-hosted clone is strictly better on privacy and strictly worse on the day your container quietly stops and you have no homepage.
notes: Start pages are the classic weekend project that people actually keep using, mostly because the requirements are entirely your own.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal browser start page. Empty folder, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, better-sqlite3 for storage in ./data/startpage.db, dnd-kit for drag and drop. Server actions or route handlers for all writes. No auth provider, no external API keys except what is listed below.

Data model: pages (id, name, sort order), widgets (id, page_id, column index, sort order, type, title, config JSON), links (id, widget_id, title, url, sort order, favicon_url). Widget types: bookmarks, note, rss, search.

UI: a top row of page tabs, then a responsive 3 column masonry-ish layout of widget cards. Drag widgets between columns and links within a bookmarks widget, persist order immediately. Inline edit for widget titles and note bodies. Add link via a small form that accepts a URL, fetches the page title server side if the title field is blank, and caches the favicon from Google's favicon service to ./public/favicons.

RSS widget: server side fetch and parse with rss-parser, show the latest 8 items as links, cache responses in SQLite for 15 minutes, never block first paint on a feed.

Search widget: a text input that submits to a configurable engine URL template, default DuckDuckGo.

Import: an /import page that accepts a browser bookmarks HTML export, parses it with cheerio, and creates one bookmarks widget per top level folder.

Export: a GET /api/export route that returns the whole database as JSON.

Dark theme by default, keyboard focus on the search box on load, and the page must render fully in under 200ms from local SQLite.

Out of scope: multi user accounts, sharing, browser extension, weather, calendar, stocks, mobile app.

Put any optional config in .env.example. Write a README with dev and Docker run instructions, and seed the database with three example widgets so the first load is not blank.
